chapter: From Pittsburgh to Maxine Sullivan: management and style
title: John Kirby as bandleader and the arrangers
summary: Kirby's band backed her on records; he handled band business and chose arrangers such as Lou Singer.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Leading a band: running, choosing and keeping players

blocks.x: Okay, can I ask you a little bit about John Kirby?
At this time your working relationship began to develop.
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943
And you - he began to back you in your records and so on. Would you tell us a little bit about what kind of person he was?

Kirby's Band, except for "Gone With The Wind", it was on all of those early recordings of mine, but my band just happened to be under the direction of Claude Thornhill, but it was Kirby's group.
Kirby began to contact different arrangements especially a Lou Singer who was a group who was working for leads usually, and I think that Kurby must have decided maybe that the singing of these classics might be a good idea for his combination, otherwise it would have been just another jazz group. And so he engage Lou Singer and then after Lou had made several arrangements and they got the sound they wanted, Charlie Shavers and Billy Kyle began to compose and make little arrangements to keep that John Kirby sound.
Kirby took care of mostly of the band business but it was actually the Charlie Shavers and Billy Kyle who were responsible for the musical ideas. And of course he had a very good group of musicians with him, Russell Procope, Buster Bailey, Charlie, Billy Kyle. So he
